you enjoy fast spell casting combat

cohorts.summary: Players find the castle visually stunning but encounter empty open spaces, brief classes, technical crashes, and forced online connectivity.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a detailed, visually stunning recreation of Hogwarts castle and an open world that is enjoyable to explore.

citations.review_text: Hogwarts Legacy is a visually stunning and immersive RPG that captures the magic of Hogwarts with breathtaking graphics, enchanting sound design, and engaging exploration, even if its storyline feels predictable at times.

I gave this game a try, but there isn't much positive I can say about it. The game feels like a single-player MMO, with an extremely generic main quest, boring side quests, and thousands of collectibles scattered across the world. None of the characters have any real charisma or personality, making it hard to care about them.

The protagonist is the generic "chosen one" who masters everything on the first attempt and excels at everything without effort. You attend Hogwarts, yet the classes themselves are reduced to short cutscenes, which completely misses the point of a game set at Hogwarts. They could have made the protagonist an Auror with amnesia, and the story would have made more sense.

The game is also very poorly optimized, although it remains playable. I don't recommend using upscaling, as it introduced visual artifacts and rendering issues that made the experience much worse. During my holidays I wanted to continue playing, but I couldn't even launch the game because of Denuvo. It's outrageous that a single-player game require a constant internet connection just to play and than game dev is crying about piracy. 

The one aspect the game absolutely gets right is Hogwarts itself. The castle is beautiful, highly detailed, and a joy to explore. It's a shame, because with better optimization and actual story this could have been a great game. Instead, it feels like an empty shell made for die-hard Harry Potter fans.

Even after just 7 hours, Hogwarts Legacy already feels like a love letter to Harry Potter fans. Exploring Hogwarts, learning spells, and flying around the world is genuinely immersive. The castle itself is packed with detail and secrets that make you want to keep exploring. Combat is surprisingly fun and fluid too.

The story starts a bit slow, but once the world opens up, it becomes hard to stop playing. If you enjoy magic, exploration, and RPG progression, this game is definitely worth experiencing.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game crashes during the shader preparation phase on PC.

citations.review_text: I enjoy the game but it is so poorly optimized for PC that it crashes constantly. Very annoying.

The state of this game is not just pathetic, its an INSULT to anyone who had the misfortune of paying for this.

For context, I first played Hogwarts Legacy on the Series S, and there it ran like a charm and looked the part too, so I ask you, how with my PC being at least twice as powerful and the game having 3 years to 'fix', does it STILL run like this?!
Im sorry, did Port Key games not get enough billions of dollars to justify ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ TRYING???

This joke of software has crashed on me more times than any Bethesda game ive ever played, ive already needed to edit the damn file setting in the Player config folder, simply to get this to run!
Yet AGAIN today when I decided to try and play (emphasis on TRY), HL decided to "prepare shaders" and once again crash 10% of the way! Im so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ over this.

The state of this release on PC is such a blatant insult to the PC gaming community that it genuinely feels personal!
The sheer fact this title made over $2 BILLION yet they clearly didnt give half a damn to even fix the PC port is INSANE!!!

If it isnt clear by now, I dont recommend you waste your money on this game, Port Key clearly didnt either!

For Context: 
Never in all my years playing on PC have I felt such frustration at the sheer lack of effort a studio has put into the state of their release, and thats coming from someone who loved Fallout and The Elder Scrolls!
Perhaps I wouldnt be so mad if the game itself was as bad as this port, but no. HL is a solid 8/10, yet this PC port is so horrid, it brings the whole score down to 3/10 and thats being generous! 

Score:
World Design: 10/10
Audio and immersion: 9/10
Character and story: 8/10
Pacing: 6/10
Performance and Optimization: -9/10

Final rating: 3/10

Id say do better Port Key, but youve clearly had enough years to prove you dont care!

citations.review_text:
**⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ 10/10 — A dream come true for every Harry Potter fan**

As a lifelong Harry Potter fan, Hogwarts Legacy is honestly one of those games I never wanted to end.

Walking through Hogwarts for the first time was something I will never forget. Seeing the castle, exploring the classrooms, discovering secret passages and simply wandering around the grounds felt incredibly magical.

This isn't just a game that uses the Harry Potter name.

It actually makes you **feel like you are part of that world.**

The attention to detail is amazing. Every corridor, painting, library and little corner of Hogwarts feels like someone genuinely cared about bringing the world to life.

And then there is the music.

Sometimes I would stop playing just to listen and look around.

Flying over the Hogwarts grounds on a broomstick, exploring Hogsmeade, discovering new locations and learning spells gave me that same feeling I had when I first watched the movies as a kid.

Of course, the game isn't perfect. Some side activities can become repetitive, and there are moments where the open world feels a little too game-like.

But honestly?

I didn't care.

Because every time I returned to Hogwarts, I felt like I was coming home.

**10/10.**

If you grew up loving Harry Potter, play this game.

Turn the lights down, put on headphones, and take your time exploring.

For a few hours, you won't just be playing a game.

**You'll be going back to Hogwarts.** 🪄

If you are a fan of Harry Potter, you will like this game. I loved it. It's an absolutely blast fighting with spells and exploring the wizarding world. The devs did a great job of giving you just enough Harry Potter references to make you love it, while not directly linking the game with the books/movies. The graphics are great, quests are interesting, flying on a broom is AWESOME, and fights are so fun. I wish there were a few more character relationships, but the few there are take a long time to progress and are worth the time and effort. The only downside to this game is that it gets VERY repetitive. I got tired of doing a million treasure dungeon dives and a million merlin trials. But with all of the things I did love, it made these annoyance less of an issue. I would give it overall a 9/10.

The game is absolutely gorgeous and delivers what it promises with all the spells,magical creatures,the dark forest,Hogsmeade etc.You get 1 Unique mission for each house.
There are only some things that i find very disappointing-
1-When you explore the different towns outside of Hogwarts Castle, there is a set number of repetitive filler tasks that makes the game feel boring and breaks immersion. Out of all these tasks, the Merlin Trials are the most annoying, especially since you have to complete hundreds of them if you want to 100% the game.
2-There is no quidditch game, i mean this is a Harry Potter game with NO QUIDDITCH! this was the most disappointing thing in this game. I hope this gets clarified if the game gets sequels.
3-The side quest that Sebastian gives you feels better than the main storyline, though the main storyline is not bad by any means.
4-For a game like this and other hogwarts(Harry Potter) games that i have played the hogwarts castle had a few no. of mysteries(excluding the repetitive ones where you need to cast a specific spell to reveal a collectible) to solve.
Overall the game is worth it.

[b] As a Harry Potter fan, this is an absolute masterpiece. [/b] This game is so addictive; once you're in, you forget about the time. I loved exploring Hogwarts; some of the details are crazy. I got completely lost in it. 

[b] The story is awesome, [/b] but with the main story, they could have done better with Sebastian. Some of the side quests are really good and interesting, but some things are way too repetitive, like the Merlin Trials. There are a lot of trials; it just feels like they are right next to each other. 

[b] Combat System is really good; [/b] it's satisfying doing combos of spells and boom-bamming enemies. Also, the most creepy thing in the game for me was that quest when you buy your own shop in Hogsmeade. Holy Guacamole, it keeps giving me chills while doing it. It was like I'm playing a horror game; that was thrilling and scary. 

[i] I hope in the next game they improve some things like optimizing the game, etc., for a smoother game. experience. [/i]

claims.claim: Reviewers report that casting Unforgivable Curses in front of professors or characters carries no meaningful consequences or reactions.

citations.review_text:
Hogwarts Legacy is an awesome and cozy game overall that delivers the ultimate wizarding school fantasy.

However, the story logic gets a little bit weird at times. You can literally cast Unforgivable Spells right in front of Hogwarts professors with zero consequences, even just a few minutes after being strictly told never to use them.

While exploring Hogwarts castle is magical, the outer open world is even worse than traditional Ubisoft open worlds. It gets bogged down by the same repetitive points of interest scattered across the map, with the only content truly worthy of your time being the unique puzzles.

Hogwarts Professors: "The Unforgivable Curses are an absolute abomination and using them will result in immediate expulsion!"
Also me: Levitating a poacher into the air, freezing them solid, and then shattering them into a thousand pieces with Diffindo before heading to Herbology class.
You do not even need to be a die hard Harry Potter fan to appreciate what an absolute achievement this game is. Though if you did grow up with the books or movies walking into the Great Hall or seeing the common rooms for the first time will genuinely give you goosebumps. It captures the pure magic of the universe in a way no game before it has ever managed.

The developers clearly poured an immense amount of love and reverence into designing the environment. The castle itself is a masterpiece, it's absolutely packed with moving portraits, hidden rooms and secrets! I spent my first several hours just wandering the corridors and taking in the atmosphere. Hogsmeade feels equally alive, bustling with chatter and backed by a phenomenal soundtrack that perfectly echoes the whimsical energy of the films.

The open world is vast and visually stunning and getting around is a blast. The broom controls are incredibly smooth and snappy to the point where flying mounts feel almost entirely redundant because the broom is just so much faster to mount and dismount.


Where the game unexpectedly excels is the spellcasting sandbox, the combat is fast, fluid and surprisingly deep. Stringing together combos like pulling an enemy close with Accio, lighting them on fire with Incendio and blasting them off a cliff with Depulso never gets old honestly. You also have access to potions and combat plants like the Chinese Chomping Cabbages (which are essentially 50% vegetable and 50% teeth) that can tear through encounters for you.

The game leans heavily into making you a one-wizard army. It’s definitely more of a beautiful relaxing journey than a brutal mountain climb; the game is very generous with its dodg…

The story is meh, the character are almost all meh. Why so linear? Why a story so boring and obvious? The only great part is the castle, where you really feel in the HP world. A part from that and the spells (super satisfying), is pretty boring. Also, the unforgivable spells have no consequences,  so unforgivable for who? Nobody reacts a part for some comments in the background.

claims.claim: Reviewers praise the detailed design and atmosphere of Hogwarts castle and Hogsmeade.

citations.review_text:
It’s hard for me to say whether I recommend it or not. Ultimately, let’s say I do, though the game has plenty of issues.

Pros:
- This game is an absolute treat for Potterheads. Hogwarts and Hogsmeade look simply fantastic. There are little details and nods to the series everywhere.
- The combat is quite engaging and enjoyable. In my opinion, the PC version could be a bit better optimized for keyboard and mouse.
- Some of the side and main storylines are quite interesting. In my opinion first half of the game is way more charming with attending classes etc.

Cons:
- [i]Revelio, Revelio, Revelio, Revelio[/i]. If players needs to constantly use some kind of special sight your exploration sucks. Period.
- Absolutely awful, disgusting, and unbearable ludonarrative dissonance. Our character is great at everything. Nothing is difficult for them. And of course they are a Chosen One. Plus, as a student who has barely started at Hogwarts, we go around killing Ashwinders, Goblins, and other magical creatures. Add to that the Unforgivable Curses, which you can cast anywhere and they don’t make an impression on anyone.
- Even though the world is filled with NPCs, it feels like a dollhouse. Non-player characters practically don’t react to anything happening around them. Open world feels equally empty. The map is enormous yet the amount of unique content is lost in its vastness.
- The open-world disease. That is, it’s filled with a handful of activities repeated dozens or even hundreds of times. Merlin’s Trials quickly become boring and repetitive. Clearing yet another enemy camp rewards us with nothing more than another trait. Catching magical beasts is just spamming an F so... Adding a mini-game to the Alohomora spell was also a terrible design choice.
- The game’s optimization leaves much to be desired, even on high-end hardware.

I maxed game achievements, but at times I had to clench my teeth as I waded through some of the developers' decisions.

Hogwarts and Hogsmeade are wonderfully crafted - the sheer amount of detail is easily the best part of the game. The music is incredible, too. You can truly feel the passion and love that went into the architecture, music, and Potter lore.

But overall? It’s a pretty mid game.

The quests and characters are unbelievably dull, and the 'plot twists' are idiotic, even for kindergarteners. Character models also look outdated and rigid. Gameplay is mid at best. Honestly, if you want a decent experience, you need to install 30+ QoL mods just to make the game feel complete.

That being said, I'm glad I played it. In fleeting moments, it still managed to capture that magical fairy-tale feeling from childhood - just like when I first read Harry Potter or watched The Chronicles of Narnia. A great part of that feeling came from Hogsmeade and Hogwarts with that beautiful music, just roaming around and taking everything in.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe performance issues including lag spikes and traversal stutters during gameplay.

citations.review_text: Still has lots of bugs but worth the hassle. Performance is not very well optimized either.

Amazing game!!!! I love it so much!!!!

I'm not a huge fan of Harry Potter, but I do love all the movies and been watching them since my childhood. I played Harry Potter The Philosopher's Stone and Chamber of secrets and I'm big fan of these!! Hogwarts Legacy feels just like my old HP games (philoshoper's stone and chamber of secrets) but much much more detailed!!! I'm having a blast!!! 
The story is awesome! The game feels like you're literally living inside Hogwarts. Im using 100 mods, there are cute mods such as clothes, and FMC (female) preset, all done very beautifully by people. The mods are installed inside the game menu, which I appreciate a lot! You can browsing any mods directly from game menu. I personally love to use Scarlet head hair mod as my female character, allowing me to play as a cute japanese young girl. wearing Burberry coat and running around Hogwarts!! wow! 

I particularly love the "cards" design of each quests icons!! 

The game runs really well, 200-250fps+ fully maxed out 2560X1600 ray tracing full + X4 frame gen. no issues at all. There are very small traversal stutters, which is common for Unreal Engine, but thanks god the game doesnt have stutters.
I do use my own Reshade + Relook, this makes the game insanely gorgeous and I might release a mod on Nexus. Basically it removes the yellow tint and makes the game to look like as it has Path Tracing. Bright surface and exceptional photorealistic lightning + LUT.  Very realistic look. However it does have a big hit, around 50-90fps (Im at 150-180fps now).

[h1]Bugs, Stutters, Heavy RAM Usage, Graphical and Sound Issues[/h1]

As a potterhead, you will love this game and play it no matter what. They did some fine job making this game, especially regarding the design of the game and its in-game environment. But after a few times playing it, you will be suffered by how this great game is a mess from within. I'm wondering where are the developers of this game and on what they are working on exactly right now? The bugs are so nerve-wrecking. The visual bugs even more! The ray-tracing is awful and it'd be only acceptable if you turn on ray reconstruction. RAM usage is on NINETY PERCENT! I had never achieved that number in any AAA game, and this game is doing whatever he can to eat up that RAM. And why?? It doesn't even work as well as a 90% RAM using game should. At one moment, the camera is focused on the character who is speaking and the moment camera comes back to your character, most of its surrounding objects are blurred out and re-rendered AGAIN! I'm wondering what is stored in the 90% then... . 
Then there goes the problem with sound. The sounds echo sometimes, and sometimes just the sound is too low on my headphone while other games are loud enough. And sometimes some SFXs simply act bug-ish like.
Again, I say that the game front-end is fine for a potterhead, but the back-end is a trash. I hope someone someday cleans this mess, because rn, the devs seems to be idling.
Runs like crap, not had any game have so many lag spikes, spent half the time playing a powerpoint

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat system as featuring fast spell combos, though some find that enemy encounters become repetitive over time.

citations.review_text: The castle is truly a thing to behold. Possibly one of the coolest single indoor structures ever put in a game. Unfortunately the game peaks there and as the campaign goes on you spend less and less time in it. The combat is fun while you learn it, but after a couple dozen hours it's rinse and repeat no matter what you are fighting. The puzzles, also fun at first, but there are dozens of near 1:1 copies of a handful of puzzle "types" that only exist to eat up your time. They simply aren't worth doing. You can easily hit max level while barely making progress in the main story which is pretty deflating. The castle itself is a masterpiece, it's absolutely packed with moving portraits, hidden rooms and secrets! I spent my first several hours just wandering the corridors and taking in the atmosphere. Hogsmeade feels equally alive, bustling with chatter and backed by a phenomenal soundtrack that perfectly echoes the whimsical energy of the films.

The open world is vast and visually stunning and getting around is a blast. The broom controls are incredibly smooth and snappy to the point where flying mounts feel almost entirely redundant because the broom is just so much faster to mount and dismount.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the open world outside of Hogwarts features repetitive side content such as Merlin Trials.

citations.review_text:
I had an amazing time playing Hogwarts Legacy, I think the approach to the story of this game was decent and I like that it expands the world to places outside of England. Despite the tediousness of locating certain Floo Network areas on the map, I do still like the Map design for the school, and I did get into a few hiccups here and there where the game would crash and I did discover a few bugs but it didn't hinder my experience.

There were a few times where I found the experience of using Alohomora to be a bit tedious, I felt that if I were to unlock better levels of Alohomora, say 'Alohomora II', I would be able to just automatically unlock the doors of every 'Alohomora I' locks. Is not as if I don't like the idea of these mini games, but when you repeatedly have to play the same mini game, with the exact same challenge over and over again, it gets rather boring. I can also say the same about the Merlin Trials, but at least there's variety, which I did enjoy.

Overall I definitely still love the game, despite its flaws. I love Harry Potter so much when I first started reading the books, the magical world is just so wonderful, and this game truly brought everything that I love about it to life. Being able to cast spells, and fight Mountain Trolls and see magical creatures, I enjoyed it a lot! If possible I'm going to try 100% this game till its completion.

9/10 - Every Harry Potter fan's dream (Even better with mods)


if you grew up wanting a hogwarts letter, just get this. walking through the castle for the first time is insane, the detail is incredible. flying on a broom and exploring the highlands feels amazing. combat is actually super fun too, pulling off spell combos makes you feel like a total badass.my only real complaints are that the open world outside hogwarts gets a bit repetitive with the merlin trials, and the gear inventory fills up way too fast.

but honestly, downloading mods gives it such an extra fun and good touch. installing quality-of-life mods fixes the annoying inventory limits, and adding silly cosmetic mods adds a hilarious twist to the game.

overall it's an absolute blast. easily one of the best wizarding games ever made, especially if you mod it.

I got 100% completion on this game, 45/45 achievements, and it got worse and worse as I played. The main story isn't compelling, and is blown way out of proportion for what a 5th year student should be dealing with. Also, it doesn't address the issue with second class citizens in the wizarding world, it just creates a simplified version: the "good" goblins in the game submit to wizarding rule, and the "bad" ones are all evil and violent and want to murder people and take power for themselves. Also, the whole ancient magic bit doesn't feel at all like a Harry Potter world story. 
Hogwarts and Hogsmeade are really well crafted and very detailed, so that's nice. The open world is way too big and ambitious, most of it is filler content like Merlin Trials which are repetitive and boring. They should have made it smaller, and focused on the side quests and bandit camps for good content.
Probably my favorite part of the game was going around the open world doing side quests. Some of these are really dark, especially Tangled Web, and they work really well. However, it doesn't make any sense that a 5th year, who just entered Hogwarts, is doing this stuff.
The combat generally isn't bad. You have the option to do some pretty fun combos, but you can also just spam damage and not try hard at all. This is a bigger problem in boss fights, where the only spells that affect them are damage spells. It quickly becomes a formula of evade attacks, wait until the boss is vulnerable, spam all damage spells quickly, then go back to step one. Very boring. They should have removed damage, and made less enemies, and given each enemy a specific combo of spells to defeat them. This would make combat more engaging, and also would feel more real(Basic cast is such a game term, it's ridiculous to hear characters say it like it's a real spell.)

Without a doubt, my favorite part of Hogwarts Legacy is the worldbuilding. The world of Hogwarts, and especially Hogwarts Castle itself, is brimming with magical charm. It's alive, mysterious... and huge! I spent so much time just exploring the winding passages, hallways, and rooms which never seemed to end. All filled with secrets and interactivity, talking paintings, suits of armor, and floating books. This applies to the wider game world as well, with its gorgeous scenery and landscapes. The music was beautiful, similarly magical and effortlessly setting the tone for the experience from the first time you load the game. Both the music and magical world reminded me quite a bit of Narnia, after which I realized how cool it would be to have a game set in Narnia from the same people responsible for this world's setting.

I was pleased to see the integrated mod support for Hogwarts Legacy. Even though I didn't make use of it during my first playthrough, I always like when games provide it. There's also plenty to do in terms of gameplay. From main & side quests, to additional content in the world, discovering the world's secrets and solving its puzzles, customizing the Room of Requirement, creature capturing/breeding, and plenty more. Some of it can be a bit repetitive, however. There's too much busywork when it comes to things like the Treasure Vaults or Merlin Trials, which offer little to no rewards past a certain point and only serve to pad out playtime. The spells and combat are varied enough to create a few interesting builds, the spells themselves are satisfying to use, and the flow of combat is engaging once you get into the flow of using your toolkit. 

The game needs a bit of polish though unfortunately. Non-story cutscenes are stilted and awkward, in both camera use and facial animations of the NPCs. Transitions from gameplay to cutscenes are often clumsy and lazy, with harsh camera cuts or cuts to black. Voice actors are reused a LOT, I think Mr. JB Bla…

136 hours later and I'd still recommend this game to pretty much anyone. Exploring Hogwarts and the rest of the world was easily my favorite part, the combat feels flashy and fun, and I spent way too much time customizing my character. The nostalgia definitely carried a lot of the experience for me. It isn't perfect though. Merlin Trials get repetitive, the gear system becomes more of a chore than anything, and it's kind of funny that nobody cares if you use the Unforgivable Curses. Still, I had a great time and I'd happily give it a 9/10.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that choices made during quests and dialogue do not significantly impact or alter the course of the story.

citations.review_text:
[h3]A fantastic game with a lot of potential for an even better sequel[/h3]

Hogwarts Legacy is, overall, a fantastic game. The graphics are beautiful, the map is huge and fun to explore, and the story is genuinely interesting. After 186 hours of gameplay, I can definitely say that I enjoyed my time with it and would recommend it to any Harry Potter fan.

That said, there are quite a few things that I wish had been developed further (not counting mods):

[list]
[*]Choices and consequences: This is probably my biggest criticism. While there are choices throughout the game, they rarely have a significant impact on the story. I would have loved for our decisions to actually change the course of events, especially considering the price of the game. It would have made different playthroughs feel much more meaningful.
[*]Magical creatures: The number of creatures available feels surprisingly limited. Any Harry Potter fan knows there are many more magical creatures that could have been included. I would have loved to see a larger variety, perhaps taking some inspiration from Hogwarts Mystery. It would also have been nice to have larger vivariums, since the number of creatures you can keep at once feels quite restrictive.
[*]Character customization: The customization options are decent, but I would have loved something much more advanced. Being able to adjust things like eye spacing, nose height, facial proportions, etc. would have made creating a truly unique character much more satisfying.
[*]Relationships:This isn't necessary for the gameplay, but I think a relationship system would have added a lot. It would have been interesting to have a relationship meter with the main characters that changed depending on your choices. Characters could then react differently to your presence or during missions depending on whether they liked or disliked you. Romance options would have been another interesting addition—not necessary, but definitely something that could have added anot…

So I just finished the game very thoroughly (level 40, 100% challenges), and I'll say overall a very solid RPG. Positives were outstanding visuals - Hogwarts itself is absolutely massive and wonderous, the world is just lovely and well laid out, and just about the right size. Spells were also very cool. I do recommend a fairly powerful video card though. 

The only real negative for me was that optional dialogue was very tedious with the two choices as to how to respond generally landed you at the same spot. There's no real way to RPG as an evil person - at worst you can occasionally be rude to someone with sometimes very mild consequences for having done so. I'd say the 2nd go around they should try to make your decisions more consequential to the point that it could improve replayability.
for "choices matter", your choices REALLY dont matter. but it can be fun, just get it on sale or from a key for like 30 bucks. the animals are sick though

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the game lacks multiplayer functionality or options to play co-operatively with friends.

citations.review_text: I'm just missing the multiplayer options but I heard there is a mod now to play multiplayer

As a huge Harry Potter fan, I absolutely loved Hogwarts Legacy. It truly captured the magic of exploring Hogwarts and the surrounding world. The castle is incredibly detailed, and I found myself getting distracted just wandering around discovering hidden rooms, puzzles, and secrets.

The combat is surprisingly fun and fast-paced, with lots of spells to unlock and combine. Flying on a broom, caring for magical beasts, and customizing my Room of Requirement made the experience even better. There was always something new to do, so it never felt repetitive.

The graphics are beautiful, the music perfectly matches the Wizarding World, and the attention to detail is amazing. It genuinely feels like you're living as a student at Hogwarts.

If you're a Harry Potter fan, this game is a dream come true. Even if you're not deeply familiar with the series, it's still an excellent open-world RPG with plenty to explore. I had an amazing time from beginning to end and would highly recommend it. The only thing I wish it had would be an online option to play with my friends.

If you’ve ever dreamed of being sorted into a house full of kind‑hearted, hard‑working, quietly‑chaotic heroes (I’m a very proud Hufflepuff, and yes, I did pet every beast I met), mastering every flavor of magic, soaring across the countryside on a broomstick, solving ancient puzzles, raising adorable magical creatures, and basically living your most wholesome wizard life… then Hogwarts Legacy is absolutely your game.

I’ve poured 178 hours into this world — and honestly, it feels like home. The exploration is warm and wonder‑filled. The spellcasting is joyful and just a little mischievous. The vibe? Pure comfort fantasy. And through it all, I wandered around in my yellow‑and‑black robes, helping everyone I could, collecting every plant, and making sure no beast went unloved.

Now, the one con — and it’s a gentle little ache — is that it’s a single‑player experience. I can only imagine how delightful it would be to explore Hogwarts with friends. Cooperative beast‑care? Cozy herbology hangouts? Broomstick picnics in the sky? The wholesome chaos would be unmatched.

But even with that one flaw, Hogwarts Legacy delivers everything I ever wanted from stepping into the magical world of Hogwarts. It’s enchanting, heartfelt, and genuinely hard to put down — especially when you’re a Hufflepuff who believes every quest deserves kindness, curiosity, and maybe a snack break.

citations.review_text:
I cannot possibly recommend this game to other people. 
I find it rather strange that after this game has been out for nearly 3 entire years, the playability get WORSE with every patch. As of July 2026, I cannot play with a controller for more than a few minutes before camera and player movement desync. Graphical glitches have also gotten quiet bad, with certain quests triggering screen blinking, or will shudder and stutter during quests. I have made attempts to play with mods to see if removing or uninstalling them or the game helps, but there are no change in crappy performance when I do.

This is not a game without faults, but overall it was a very fun experience that I would recommend. If you're going into this for the story, you may be disappointed; I found the dialogue to be pretty low quality and borderline cringe at times. But the game makes up for it with an extensive world to explore, generally good combat, and many surprising features to find along the way. Definitely worth grabbing during a sale. (and it goes on sale fairly often!) 
Be warned! I encountered a technical glitch OFTEN while playing this game. This game does have an optimization issue for clearing VRAM, which causes the game to start flickering after about 1.5-2 hours into a gaming session. VERY frustrating, lowering the graphics did NOT help, and this problem only gets worse the further you get into the game. HOWEVER, if you can bear with this, it's still a fun game to play. But developers, PLEASE fix this!
